name: Propofol
drug_class: Intravenous general anaesthetic and sedative emulsion
high_alert_note: Named as a high-risk infusion example in the FDA infusion pump page; the local high-alert list governs.
summary: Intravenous general anaesthetic and sedation drug; ICU sedation of intubated, mechanically ventilated adults is among its labelled indications. Nursing focus: strict aseptic handling, cardiovascular depression, hypersensitivity and propofol infusion syndrome.
evidence_type_note: The evidence here is a regulator product label (prescribing information written for prescribers and pharmacists). It is not a bedside nursing practice guideline: the nursing actions are inferences from label warnings, marked partial, and the unit's protocol governs practice.
jurisdiction_note: US FDA label only. EMA, MHRA and SFDA labels were not read; indications, warnings and presentations differ by country and by manufacturer.

items.text: The label describes propofol injectable emulsion as an intravenous general anaesthetic and sedation drug, with indications that include ICU sedation of intubated, mechanically ventilated adult patients.

Strict aseptic technique must be maintained; vials are never accessed more than once or used for more than one person; administration should start promptly and be completed within the time the label states; discard unused product and do not use it if contamination is suspected.
Follow the unit's aseptic handling rules for every lipid emulsion product and report any suspected contamination.
Sedation scoring, haemodynamic and respiratory monitoring follow the unit's sedation protocol.
Serious and sometimes fatal hypersensitivity reactions can occur.
Bradycardia, asystole and cardiac arrest have been reported; the label warns of cardiovascular depression and hypotension.
Propofol infusion syndrome is described among the label's serious adverse reactions.
The label lists hypersensitivity, hypotension and bradycardia and propofol infusion syndrome among the serious adverse reactions discussed in its warnings.
Escalate immediately for hypotension, bradycardia, signs of allergy, unexplained metabolic or cardiac deterioration, or suspected contamination.
Record sedation scores, haemodynamics, product handling and escalation per unit standard.
Institution-specific preparation: follow your pharmacy's preparation standard and the product labelling. This library gives no preparation or concentration instructions.
Institution-specific dosing: follow the prescriber's order and your institution's approved protocol. This library gives no dosing instructions.

monitoring.text: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure at the unit's frequency during sedation.
Assess sedation depth with the unit's validated tool.
Handle the product with strict aseptic technique and never re-access a vial.
Report bradycardia, hypotension, allergic signs or suspected contamination immediately.
